nodes.label: dpm-core feature gates must only wrap impl blocks, never struct fields
nodes.rationale: Workspace feature unification makes single-crate compilation behave differently from whole-workspace compilation if struct fields are gated; the project was previously broken this way, so feature gates must stay additive and impl-only.
nodes.norm_label: dpm-core feature gates must only wrap impl blocks, never struct fields

nodes.label: zip_folder/unzip_file/hasher duplicated independently in dpm and dpm-server
nodes.rationale: Neither crate shares this logic through dpm-core; client and server unzip_file signatures have already drifted apart (client is missing a name parameter), so edits to one copy must be manually mirrored to the other until consolidated.
nodes.norm_label: zip_folder/unzip_file/hasher duplicated independently in dpm and dpm-server

nodes.label: json_parse1.rs is pre-split dead code not wired into main.rs mod tree
nodes.rationale: Left over from before the three repos were split/merged; risk is a developer mistakenly editing the dead copy instead of the real dpm_core types.
nodes.norm_label: json_parse1.rs is pre-split dead code not wired into main.rs mod tree

nodes.label: turso version pinned to 0.6.1 in dpm to match geni's internal pin
nodes.rationale: geni internally pins turso 0.6.1; if dpm's own turso dependency diverges, two copies of turso link into one binary, causing turso_sdk_kit C ABI symbol duplication (linker failure) and mimalloc #[global_allocator] conflicts. Must be bumped in lockstep whenever geni updates.
nodes.norm_label: turso version pinned to 0.6.1 in dpm to match geni's internal pin

nodes.label: Shallow clone whole repo instead of true git sparse-checkout for source packages
nodes.rationale: git2/libgit2's sparse-checkout support is less mature than the git CLI's; since source-kind repos are expected to be small text files, trading bandwidth for a simpler, reliable API is an accepted simplification until large source repos make it worth revisiting.
nodes.norm_label: shallow clone whole repo instead of true git sparse-checkout for source packages

nodes.label: drop_privileges_for_build is the load-bearing safeguard against root-executed build commands
nodes.rationale: On Linux, --system scope re-execs the whole dpm process as root via sudo::escalate_if_needed(); without explicitly dropping privileges (via SUDO_UID/SUDO_GID) before spawning the build command, an arbitrary third-party shell command would run as root. This mechanism must never be removed or bypassed without re-establishing an equivalent guarantee.
nodes.norm_label: drop_privileges_for_build is the load-bearing safeguard against root-executed build commands

nodes.label: repo_init (rebuild RepoInfo.json by rescanning local zips) deleted, not rewritten
nodes.rationale: Once binary hosting moves external, the local filesystem no longer has enough information (url/hash were only known at publish time) to reconstruct the index by rescanning; the premise repo_init depended on no longer holds.
nodes.norm_label: repo_init (rebuild repoinfo.json by rescanning local zips) deleted, not rewritten

nodes.label: publish.yml's role is smaller than the spec's original bot-commit-back model
nodes.rationale: fix add --url requires a human-supplied external hosting URL that CI has no way to discover on its own, so there is no bot-commit-to-main step to automate; publish.yml is reduced to a read-only post-merge sanity re-check of RepoInfo.json's shape, needing no PAT.
nodes.norm_label: publish.yml's role is smaller than the spec's original bot-commit-back model

nodes.label: 'Latest version' means highest rowid (insertion order), not semver comparison
nodes.rationale: dpm update always clears and refills a source's table, so insertion order equals RepoInfo.json array order equals publish order; adding a real semver dependency now would be an unused dependency until Phase 5 (pubgrub) actually needs version comparison.
nodes.norm_label: 'latest version' means highest rowid (insertion order), not semver comparison

nodes.label: A dependency name with no source field cannot be disambiguated by the depending package's author
nodes.rationale: Dependency{name,version} has no source field; resolving which source a bare dependency name refers to reuses the same 0/1/2+-sources rule as top-level CLI targets, so a name ambiguous across sources fails with AmbiguousPackage with no way for the package author to pin it — a real, permanent limitation noted for TODO.md rather than solved via a schema change in this phase.
nodes.norm_label: a dependency name with no source field cannot be disambiguated by the depending package's author

nodes.label: install() unwraps on malicious/corrupt downloaded zip content, causing a panic
nodes.rationale: read_file_from_zip(...).unwrap()/JsonStorage::from_str_to(...).unwrap() assume packageInfo.json/hashes.json always exist and are well-formed; bad server data, network corruption, or a malicious repo crashes the client instead of failing gracefully.
nodes.norm_label: install() unwraps on malicious/corrupt downloaded zip content, causing a panic

nodes.label: system.rs init() never writes repo_url/repo_info back to config.json
nodes.rationale: config.json is created as literally '{}' and the default values only ever live in the in-memory HashMap; missing the JsonStorage::to_json(&config, &config_path) write-back step means every subsequent run reads a config missing these keys.
nodes.norm_label: system.rs init() never writes repo_url/repo_info back to config.json

nodes.label: PackageManager::Unknown / unsupported OS branches use panic! instead of returning an error
nodes.rationale: Seven call sites in system.rs abort the whole process on an undetected package manager or non-Linux/macOS OS instead of surfacing a ClientResult error.
nodes.norm_label: packagemanager::unknown / unsupported os branches use panic! instead of returning an error

nodes.label: Db::execute_query/drop_table/clear_table build SQL via format! with unescaped table names
nodes.rationale: Currently only ever called with the hardcoded literal 'LocalRepo', but the API has no whitelist/escaping, so any future call site passing user input as a table name would be a SQL injection vector.
nodes.norm_label: db::execute_query/drop_table/clear_table build sql via format! with unescaped table names

nodes.label: diesel.toml migrations_directory pointed at a pre-split absolute path that no longer exists
nodes.rationale: Made moot once the turso/geni migration plan deleted diesel.toml/schema.rs entirely and replaced the migration mechanism, but was an active footgun before that.
nodes.norm_label: diesel.toml migrations_directory pointed at a pre-split absolute path that no longer exists

nodes.label: Inconsistent ownership model: Linux chown root:root vs macOS chown user:admin
nodes.rationale: The two platforms end up with different post-install ownership/management semantics for --system installs; flagged as worth unifying but explicitly left untouched by the client-source-install plan, which only inherits the existing behavior.
nodes.norm_label: inconsistent ownership model: linux chown root:root vs macos chown user:admin

nodes.label: git2 declared but unused dead dependency in dpm's Cargo.toml
nodes.rationale: Originally listed alongside rusqlite/dotenv/digest/flate2/hex-literal as unused; resolved specifically for git2 once clone_package_source (client-source-install plan Task 3) started using it for real.
nodes.norm_label: git2 declared but unused dead dependency in dpm's cargo.toml

nodes.label: dpm-core's own Cargo.toml version is decoupled from the workspace version
nodes.rationale: dpm-core hardcodes version = '0.1.2' instead of version.workspace = true (0.1.0) like dpm/dpm-server; needs confirmation whether this is intentional (independent crates.io publish cadence) or an oversight.
nodes.norm_label: dpm-core's own cargo.toml version is decoupled from the workspace version

nodes.label: dpm-core README's add_package example no longer matches the real function signature
nodes.rationale: The README example passed 6 positional args, but RepoInfo::add_package now needs 8 (adding entry/description); fixed later by the multi-source-namespace plan's Task 1 Step 7, which rewrote the example around add_package_version.
nodes.norm_label: dpm-core readme's add_package example no longer matches the real function signature

nodes.label: Test/dev fixture packages (test/test1/test2/helloWorld) sit alongside real repo data in dpm-server/Repo
nodes.rationale: These 4KB dev-time fixtures look like real installable packages sitting directly in the 'official' Repo directory structure, risking confusion about what's actually a real published package.
nodes.norm_label: test/dev fixture packages (test/test1/test2/helloworld) sit alongside real repo data in dpm-server/repo
